title: Development of automated machine learning models in predicting colorectal adenoma in metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease.
summary: In 506 patients with ultrasound-confirmed metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease, the study compared logistic regression and four H2O AutoML models for colorectal adenoma. The gradient-boosting model had AUC 0.791, accuracy 0.735, sensitivity 0.754 and specificity 0.714. This cohort-specific result does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: The study compared four H2O AutoML classifiers with logistic-regression prediction for colorectal adenoma in patients with metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease; gradient boosting had the highest reported AUC.
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

evidence.tested: The H2O AutoML gradient-boosting model predicted colorectal adenoma in patients with metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease with AUC 0.791 and accuracy 0.735 in the study evaluation. Its single-study results require further validation.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and prospective real-world benefit are not established in the reviewed study.
